basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 35.' and it opens 'VERS. 35.-- Dixitque Jacob: Descendam ad filium meum lugens in infernum. Quomodo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 35.-- Dixitque Jacob: Descendam ad filium meum lugens in infernum. Quomodo intelligitur quod | Jacob dicit: Quoniam descendam ad filium meum lugens in infernum? Perturbati et dolentis verba sunt, mala sua etiam hinc exaggerantis. Vel etiam inferni nomine sepulcrum significavit: quasi dixisset: In luctu maneo donec me terrae suscipiat [Z., suscipiet] sepulcrum sicut illum.
